title: Check baby's passport or ID
note: Travelling abroad? Your baby needs their own passport. HM Passport Office says it usually takes up to 3 weeks, and longer if they need more information, so there's no harm starting early. Not in the UK? Check your own passport office.

link.label: See documents on the packing list

title: Get travel insurance that covers baby
note: Check that your baby is named on the policy, and that it covers medical treatment, hospital stays and getting home if you need to. A GHIC or EHIC card is handy but isn't a replacement for insurance.

title: Mention the trip to your GP, health visitor or paediatrician
note: Especially for a very young baby, a baby with a health condition, or a destination that needs vaccinations. Ask about medicines you can bring too.

title: Book your seats
note: Ask about bassinet seats, infant fares and what baby gear travels free before you pay.

title: Book your train seats
note: Ask about seats with a table, space for a stroller and where the baby-changing toilets are.

link.label: Questions to ask the train company

title: Book somewhere to stay
note: A cot, blackout curtains and a fridge make a bigger difference than a fancy pool.

link.label: Questions to ask the hotel or host

title: Decide on the car seat
note: Bring yours, hire one, or skip cars at the destination. Whatever you choose, sort it before you go.

link.label: Questions to ask car hire and taxis

title: Plan the route and the stops
note: Look for services or towns where you can stop for feeds and nappy changes. Shorter driving days are fine.

title: Do a practice run
note: A day out with the full nappy bag, or a nap in the travel cot at home. You'll find out what you really use.

title: Sketch out the travel day
note: Line up naps, feeds and the journey so there are fewer surprises on the day.

title: Start your packing list
note: Tick off what you already have and order anything missing while there's still time for delivery.

title: Check the baggage rules for baby gear
note: Stroller, car seat, travel cot, milk and food: what can go in the cabin, and what goes in the hold?

title: Check the time difference
note: If you're crossing time zones, you can start nudging bedtime a few days before you leave.

title: Pack the bags
note: Main bags first, nappy bag last. Charge the tablet and download shows and white noise for offline use.

title: Get the night before sorted
note: Check in online if you can, lay out travel outfits, fill the nappy bag, and put documents in one place.

title: Travel day
note: Something will go off-plan, and that's normal. Have a quick look at the meltdown guide so it's fresh in your mind.
